summary.text: imdUSD combines an Ethereum borrowing protocol, INFER staking and an app for paid AI work, according to the project’s documentation.
The project names miyagod.eth as founder; a wallet requiring two of three signatures controls settings, with changes delayed 48 hours.
Users connect a wallet, deposit staked IMD and borrow dollar-targeted imdUSD, paying transaction fees and annual interest of 4.44%.
The project says loan interest and swap surcharges reach its Treasury, which buys INFER for staking rewards.
INFER staking gives holders shares in a vault; callers trigger reward releases and receive 1% of each release.
INFER BOX accepts imdUSD for AI requests and quotes a 5% Treasury fee, the project says.
About $219,300 was locked on November 23, according to DefiLlama; the chain showed about 55,041 imdUSD issued.
The documented oracle thresholds still disagree with deployed settings, leaving conflicting descriptions of how collateral prices are accepted.

differs.why: The documentation reports deployment at block 26166417; the successful creation receipt and CREATE2 calculation establish block 26166419.
The documentation describes a minimum of 25 agents for these feeds; each deployed feed enforces at least 100.
The documentation describes 15 agreeing agents; each deployed feed enforces at least 51.
DefiLlama describes exactly 100 agents per price; a minimum of 100 does not establish the actual size of every panel.
The earlier audit brief describes one cold governor key; deployed settings name a Safe. These may describe different revisions.
The project describes revenue-funded INFER purchases, while the vault has no automatic buyback. Treasury withdrawals and permissionless reward releases do not establish who performs purchases.
The November 9 blog said no outside audit had occurred; the later repository lists public IdentityMD panels, while expressly excluding audit firms. The dated blog is retained with an outdates link.
CoinGecko reports no active trades, while DEX Screener reports ten trades in its latest window; differing coverage and observation windows remain possible.
The main Build page offers 20 checks daily; BOX API documentation describes 30 shared daily evaluations. The public sources do not explain whether these are separate entry paths or stale limits.
The website quotes a 5% service charge, but the payment contract accepts caller-selected amounts. This describes service pricing, not an enforced on-chain rate.

Who controls the two governing Safe owners other than the deploying wallet? No real-world identity is inferred from wallet or screen-name similarities.

What organizational or legal entity operates the apps? The sources name a founder and public accounts, but do not establish an incorporated operator.
